topic_title: The Army Knows Where They're Buried

slides.headline: The Army Knows Where They're Buried
slides.body: Guatemala's military waged war on its own people for 36 years. Its archives on the missing remain sealed.

slides.headline: A 36-Year War on Mayan Villages
slides.body: From 1960 to 1996, Guatemala's army fought leftist guerrillas — and massacred Indigenous communities accused of aiding them.

slides.headline: Peace Came. The Files Stayed Shut.
slides.body: The 1996 accords promised truth. Thirty years later, the Armed Forces have never opened their wartime archives.

slides.headline: UN Demands the Barracks Open
slides.body: In July 2026, UN experts Aua Balde and Ana Lorena Delgadillo Perez urged Guatemala to open every military base and archive.

slides.headline: Mothers Still Dig for Answers
slides.body: Forensic teams keep exhuming mass graves. Families search for children taken decades ago, with no state record to guide them.

slides.headline: Who Still Protects the Files?
slides.body: The generals who fought that war are aging. Every year the archives stay sealed, fewer answers survive with them.
